Parallel metadata reports codex parallel mode, actual parallel use, four subagents, successful process and artifact validation, and failed official solution status with 20 of 40 cases passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main projected trajectory shows parent probing CLI and Base58 behavior, writing and later reconciling /output, verifying samples and help, then reporting the final nested module tree.

Root raw trajectory shows initial probing, spawning Base58 and argparse children, parent implementation, waits, explicit child interruptions, unexpected /output change inspection, pruning, final verification, and final answer.

Base58 child trajectory probes executable behavior, spawns a nested argparse child, writes a full nested /output implementation, validates samples, receives interruption, and never reaches a normal final handoff.

Argparse child trajectory probes workspace and parser behavior, attempts nested spawning, writes another full /output implementation including test19.mjs, validates some cases, and is interrupted before final completion.
Nested argparse child remains read-only, probes CLI behavior, confirms parser findings including duplicates and order independence, and returns a final findings report to its parent child.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same ESM .mjs Node migration, manual argv parsing, no external dependencies, and executable-only behavioral probing.
Serial metadata reports codex serial mode, no parallel uptake or subagents, successful process and artifact validation, and failed official solution status with 19 of 40 cases passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Main serial trajectory shows one actor probing source and executable behavior, creating a flat library layout, patching Base58 integer handling, verifying sample diffs, and delivering final files.

Raw serial trajectory contains the single-agent implementation path, direct source read, executable probes, file additions and updates, sample verification, and final response without subagent activity.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the core task: port argparse and base58 behavior to pure ESM .mjs files in /output with manual argv parsing and no external npm dependencies.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent delegated Base58 and argparse probing, while children also performed implementation in the shared /output tree; no isolation or exclusive deliverable owner was maintained.
parallel.implementation: Final artifact used a nested library tree with base58 core/check modules, crypto SHA-256, encoding helpers, Python byte repr formatting, argparse-like CLI parsing, and test19.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened through shared filesystem side effects: parent first wrote a flat implementation, child agents wrote nested implementations, and parent later pruned and edited the final tree.
parallel.verification: Parent and children ran sample comparisons and CLI/error checks against the bundled executable; final parent checks included sample diffs and help output, but official hidden evaluation still failed 20 of 40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Two active child trajectories were interrupted before normal final return, and the final code still failed half of official cases despite sample-level verification.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual argv, output-format, and executable-probing requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without delegation or shared-agent ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: Created a flatter module split with bytes, hash, base58, cli, and test19.mjs; later updated base58 integer behavior after discovering a negative-integer quirk.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same actor wrote and modified the final /output files and delivered them directly, with no cross-agent merge or overwrite episode.
serial.verification: Ran all four sample diffs plus help, missing-argument, invalid-int, unknown-argument, and --arg=value checks; official hidden evaluation still failed 21 of 40 cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No child lifecycle remained open, but the implementation still missed hidden evaluator behavior and did not pass the official task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized ESM, .mjs output, manual argv parsing, Base58/Base58Check behavior, no npm dependencies, and executable-based probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and also read the mounted source script directly before implementing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement coverage was broadly similar; parallel initially relied more on probes and delegated investigation, while serial kept the requirement interpretation in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned Base58 and argparse children and later had children writing implementation files as well as probing behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for probing, implementation, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split work but did not keep exclusive ownership of the required deliverable, while serial maintained a single coherent owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel handoffs were opaque in the available raw trace and the live actors lacked an observable file-ownership contract for /output/test19.mjs and library paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff or interface boundary; the same actor kept source, parser, Base58, and output-format context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material context/interface difference is the parallel shared-workspace boundary, not a proven missing task requirement in a child brief.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final code used a nested module tree with base58, crypto, encoding, cli, io, and test19.mjs files, after competing parent and child implementations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final code used a smaller flat module tree and patched base58 integer handling after additional probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered a more hierarchical tree and slightly higher official count, while serial delivered a simpler tree; both sample-verified implementations missed hidden behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent waited on child agents, received timeouts, interrupted two still-running children, and proceeded without their normal final handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle and completed its local todo list and final response in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an adverse child result lifecycle; serial had none because all work stayed local.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Multiple live agents wrote /output/test19.mjs and overlapping library trees; the parent later noticed an unexpected entry change, pruned files, and kept the nested tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and updated one /output tree without live cross-agent file replacement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integration occurred through shared-state overwrite and cleanup, while serial integration was direct and single-owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel checked samples, help, and selected CLI behavior after reconciling output; the official evaluator completed and failed with 20/40 passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial checked all samples and several parser cases; the official evaluator completed and failed with 19/40 passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on sample and edge-case probes that were insufficient for hidden tests; parallel had one more official passing case but still failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 550 agent seconds, 129 LLM requests, four subagent rollouts, multiple waits, and closed after interrupting children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent 340 agent seconds and 24 LLM requests with no subagents or delegation waits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel carried substantially more coordination overhead and open child lifecycle cleanup; serial used less budget and had simpler closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solutions failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome to explain. Parallel passed 20 of 40 and serial passed 19 of 40. The process difference is coordination: parallel delegated probes and implementation into children, interrupted active children, and reconciled shared /output overwrites; serial kept one local implementation flow. Those parallel patterns are adverse process evidence but do not establish an outcome-differential root cause because both delivered sample-passing but hidden-test-failing ports.
parallel_contributors: Child agents wrote and replaced the shared required output tree while the parent was also implementing and verifying.
The parent interrupted active Base58 and argparse children before normal final return.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained ownership of implementation, verification, and delivery.
Serial also failed hidden tests, so its simpler process was not sufficient for success.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered a nested module hierarchy and passed one additional official testcase.
Serial delivered a flatter module hierarchy and explicitly patched negative integer Base58 behavior after probing.
Both verification sets were sample-heavy and did not expose all official hidden failures.
evaluator_effects: Only aggregate official pass counts are mounted in the pair, so hidden testcase-specific causes are not directly observable here.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse process patterns with no official outcome differential
